topics.justification: Top terms like "understand", "paper", "explain", "learn", and "math" indicate posts asking for conceptual explanations of cryptographic algorithms and their security assumptions.

Words such as "byte", "digit", "field", "polynomial", "modulo", "multiply", and "operation" point to coding questions about performing arithmetic (often GF/finite-field or big-integer modular ops) correctly and efficiently.

High-weight terms "prime", "factor", "modulus", "bit", "test", "generate", and "random" reflect number-theory tasks central to crypto: primality testing, choosing sizes, generating primes, and factoring-related feasibility.

Dominant "bit" plus "round", "box", "xor", "permutation", "block", and "constant" suggests discussions of block-cipher internals and implementation details like constant-time operations relevant to certain attacks.

topics.topic_name: Public-Key Encryption, Hashing, and Key Usage
topics.justification: Terms like "encryption", "public_key", "private_key", "ciphertext", "plaintext", "hash", "signature", and "secure" indicate questions about applying cryptographic primitives and managing keys for secure message exchange.
